title: Conquer or of Forest
statementMd:
Define the unique *ornamental* coloring of a rooted tree$^{\text{∗}}$ as the following vertex coloring:

- A vertex $v$ is colored white if the number of vertices in the subtree$^{\text{†}}$ rooted at $v$ is even;
- Otherwise, $v$ is colored black.

On his quest to conquer a forest of Christmas trees, Yuuki encountered an *ornamentally* colored tree $T$ with $n$ vertices labeled from $1$ to $n$, rooted at vertex $1$.

Yuuki considers the tree *conquered* if and only if **at least one** of the following conditions holds:

- There are no white vertices in the tree, or
- There exists some vertex $v$ such that all white vertices lie on the simple path from the root $1$ to $v$.

To *conquer* the tree, Yuuki can apply the following operation on $T$ an arbitrary number of times (possibly zero):

- First, choose a vertex $w$ that is colored white and is **not** the root of $T$. Let $p_w$ be the parent of $w$.
- Then, remove the edge connecting $p_w$ and $w$, and add an edge between **any** two vertices such that $T$ remains a tree.
- Finally, recolor the vertices of $T$ such that it is *ornamentally* colored. Note that $T$ is always rooted at vertex $1$.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6531fb7f6eb29b4dc2070d58cdb89213095b5957.png) A possible application of the operation in the first test case. The resulting tree is *conquered* since all white vertices lie on the path between vertices $1$ and $3$.

Compute the number of distinct$^{\text{‡}}$ *conquered* trees that Yuuki can construct by applying the above operation an arbitrary number of times on $T$. Since the answer may be large, output it modulo $998\,244\,353$.

Note that Yuuki cannot stop midway through an operation (in particular, he must recolor the tree before checking if it is *conquered*). Additionally, Yuuki is allowed to apply the operation even if the tree is already *conquered*.

$^{\text{∗}}$A tree is a connected graph without cycles. $^{\text{†}}$A subtree of vertex $v$ is the subgraph of $v$, all its descendants, and all the edges between them. $^{\text{‡}}$Two trees are considered distinct if and only if there exists a pair of vertices such that there is an edge between them in one of the trees, and not in the other.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $t$ ($1 \le t \le 10^4$). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer $n$ ($2\le n\le 2\cdot 10^5$) — the number of vertices in $T$.

Then $n-1$ lines follow, the $i$-th line containing two integers $u_i$ and $v_i$ ($1\le u_i \lt v_i\le n$) — the two vertices that the $i$-th edge connects.

It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $n$ over all test cases does not exceed $2\cdot 10^5$.

## Output

For each test case, output a single integer — the number of distinct *conquered* trees that can be constructed from $T$, modulo $998\,244\,353$.

## Note

In the first test case, below are the four *conquered* trees that can be constructed and a sequence of operations that constructs each one.

ExplanationIllustration The operation is applied zero times. The given tree is already *conquered* since all white vertices lie on the simple path between vertices $1$ and $4$. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/60bb572a089aa99f23441a3669087263b4106c33.png) The first and only operation selects $w$ to be vertex $3$ ($p_w$ is vertex $1$) and draws an edge between vertices $2$ and $4$. The resulting tree is *conquered* since all white vertices lie on the simple path between vertices $1$ and $3$. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bfbff514e8f9850b150399f0238c506e3e162889.png) The first and only operation selects $w$ to be vertex $3$ ($p_w$ is vertex $1$) and draws an edge between vertices $2$ and $3$. The resulting tree is *conquered* since all white vertices lie on the simple path between vertices $1$ and $3$. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b35a2f73e12b7bcc23175dde2118932c216f32b6.png) The first operation selects $w$ to be vertex $3$ ($p_w$ is vertex $1$) and draws an edge between vertices $2$ and $4$. The second operation selects $w$ to be vertex $4$ ($p_w$ is vertex $2$) and draws an edge between vertices $1$ and $4$. The resulting tree is *conquered* since all white vertices lie on the simple path between vertices $1$ and $4$. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/21d834b8929ce8a07a89faf15ad4a231e2fc130d.png)

In the second test case, Yuuki cannot apply the operation on $T$ since there are no white vertices. Additionally, $T$ is already *conquered* since there are no white vertices. Thus, the answer is $1$.
statementZhMd:
定义有根树$^{\text{∗}}$的唯一的*装饰*染色为如下的顶点染色：

- 若以 $v$ 为根的子树$^{\text{†}}$中的顶点个数为偶数，则顶点 $v$ 被染成白色；
- 否则，$v$ 被染成黑色。

在征服圣诞树森林的旅途中，Yuuki 遇到了一棵以*装饰*方式染色的树 $T$，它有 $n$ 个顶点，编号从 $1$ 到 $n$，以顶点 $1$ 为根。

当且仅当**至少一个**下列条件成立时，Yuuki 认为这棵树是*被征服*的：

- 树中没有白色顶点；或者
- 存在某个顶点 $v$，使得所有白色顶点都位于从根 $1$ 到 $v$ 的简单路径上。

为了*征服*这棵树，Yuuki 可以对 $T$ 施行以下操作任意多次（也可以零次）：

- 首先，选择一个被染成白色且**不是** $T$ 的根的顶点 $w$。设 $p_w$ 为 $w$ 的父亲。
- 然后，删除连接 $p_w$ 与 $w$ 的边，并在**任意**两个顶点之间添加一条边，使得 $T$ 仍然是一棵树。
- 最后，重新对 $T$ 的顶点进行染色，使其成为*装饰*染色。注意 $T$ 始终以顶点 $1$ 为根。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6531fb7f6eb29b4dc2070d58cdb89213095b5957.png) 第一个测试用例中操作的一种可能应用。得到的树是*被征服*的，因为所有白色顶点都位于顶点 $1$ 和 $3$ 之间的路径上。

计算 Yuuki 通过对 $T$ 施行上述操作任意多次所能构造出的不同的$^{\text{‡}}$*被征服*的树的数量。由于答案可能很大，请输出其对 $998\,244\,353$ 取模后的结果。

注意 Yuuki 不能在操作进行到一半时停止（特别地，在检查树是否*被征服*之前，他必须先重新对树染色）。此外，即使树已经*被征服*，Yuuki 也被允许继续施行操作。

$^{\text{∗}}$树是不含环的连通图。$^{\text{†}}$顶点 $v$ 的子树是由 $v$ 及其所有后代以及它们之间的所有边构成的子图。$^{\text{‡}}$当且仅当存在一对顶点，它们在其中一棵树中有边相连而在另一棵中没有边相连时，这两棵树才被视为不同。

## 输入格式

每个测试包含多个测试用例。第一行包含测试用例的个数 $t$（$1 \le t \le 10^4$）。接下来是各测试用例的描述。

每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 $n$（$2\le n\le 2\cdot 10^5$）—— 表示 $T$ 中顶点的个数。

接下来 $n-1$ 行，第 $i$ 行包含两个整数 $u_i$ 和 $v_i$（$1\le u_i \lt v_i\le n$）—— 表示第 $i$ 条边所连接的两个顶点。

保证给定的边构成一棵树。

保证所有测试用例的 $n$ 之和不超过 $2\cdot 10^5$。

## 输出格式

对于每个测试用例，输出一个整数 —— 从 $T$ 出发能够构造出的不同的*被征服*的树的数量，对 $998\,244\,353$ 取模。

## 说明

在第一个测试用例中，下面给出了可以构造出的四棵*被征服*的树，以及构造出其中每一棵的一个操作序列。

解释/图示 操作施行零次。给定的树已经*被征服*，因为所有白色顶点都位于顶点 $1$ 和 $4$ 之间的简单路径上。 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/60bb572a089aa99f23441a3669087263b4106c33.png) 第一次也是唯一一次操作选择 $w$ 为顶点 $3$（$p_w$ 为顶点 $1$），并在顶点 $2$ 和 $4$ 之间连出一条边。得到的树是*被征服*的，因为所有白色顶点都位于顶点 $1$ 和 $3$ 之间的简单路径上。 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bfbff514e8f9850b150399f0238c506e3e162889.png) 第一次也是唯一一次操作选择 $w$ 为顶点 $3$（$p_w$ 为顶点 $1$），并在顶点 $2$ 和 $3$ 之间连出一条边。得到的树是*被征服*的，因为所有白色顶点都位于顶点 $1$ 和 $3$ 之间的简单路径上。 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b35a2f73e12b7bcc23175dde2118932c216f32b6.png) 第一次操作选择 $w$ 为顶点 $3$（$p_w$ 为顶点 $1$），并在顶点 $2$ 和 $4$ 之间连出一条边。第二次操作选择 $w$ 为顶点 $4$（$p_w$ 为顶点 $2$），并在顶点 $1$ 和 $4$ 之间连出一条边。得到的树是*被征服*的，因为所有白色顶点都位于顶点 $1$ 和 $4$ 之间的简单路径上。 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/21d834b8929ce8a07a89faf15ad4a231e2fc130d.png)

在第二个测试用例中，由于树中没有白色顶点，Yuuki 无法对 $T$ 施行操作。此外，由于没有白色顶点，$T$ 已经是*被征服*的。因此，答案为 $1$。
